content: 1. For bacterial pericarditis caused by Mycoplasma pneumoniae, the recommended treatment is either ceftriaxone at a dose of 5 mg/kg administered intravenously every 6 hours for 14 to 42 days, or ampicillin-sulbactam at a dose of 3 g administered intravenously every 6 hours for 14 to 42 days. 2. For bacterial pericarditis caused by Legionella pneumophila, the preferred treatment options include ciprofloxacin at a dose of 400 mg administered intravenously every 12 hours for 14 to 42 days, or levofloxacin at a dose of 500–750 mg administered intravenously every 24 hours for 14 to 42 days, or azithromycin at a dose of 500 mg administered intravenously every 24 hours for 14 to 42 days. 3. For viral pericarditis caused by cytomegalovirus (CMV), the recommended regimen involves immunoglobulin therapy. This includes a dose of 4 mL/kg administered once daily on days 0, 4, and 8, followed by a reduced dose of 2 mL/kg on days 12 and 16. 4. For viral pericarditis caused by Coxsackie B virus, the preferred treatment is interferon alpha or beta at a dose of 2.5 million international units (Mio. IU) administered subcutaneously three times per week.
